CHIEF COMPLAINT
Positive hepatitis C antibody test found on routine physical screening.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male presenting with newly discovered positive hepatitis C antibody on routine laboratory work during annual physical. Patient reports feeling well and was surprised by the positive result. He denies any prior diagnosis of hepatitis C. Patient has a significant past history of intravenous drug use but reports being clean for over 15 years. He denies known exposure to hepatitis C partners.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies jaundice, abdominal pain, or other hepatic symptoms. No constitutional symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No significant past medical history other than positive hepatitis C screening.

MEDICATIONS
Patient denies current medications.

ALLERGIES
Not documented in this visit.

FAMILY HISTORY
Family history significant for hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and depression.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports former intravenous drug use, clean for over 15 years. Alcohol use: occasionally drinks beer daily, decreased from previous heavy use. Tobacco use: current smoker, 1-2 cigarettes per day, has significantly reduced. Patient is married with children.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: reviewed and within normal limits. General: no distress, no jaundice. Cardiovascular: regular rate and rhythm with a 2/6 systolic ejection murmur. Pulmonary: lungs clear without wheezes, rales, or rhonchi. Abdomen: bowel sounds present, soft, no hepatosplenomegaly. Neurological/Musculoskeletal: no gait disturbance or edema.

RESULTS
HCV antibody: positive. Liver panel: AST elevated at 39 U/L; ALT, albumin, and total bilirubin within normal limits.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Hepatitis C infection. Patient counseled that hepatitis C is a viral infection affecting the liver, likely present for several years, and that most patients remain asymptomatic until years later. Plan: (1) Confirm diagnosis with additional blood work including HCV RNA and HCV genotype; (2) Determine severity of liver disease with liver elastography ultrasound; (3) Screen family members (wife and children) with HCV antibody testing; (4) Arrange appointments with family doctor for family screening; (5) Follow-up visit in 3 weeks to review results and determine treatment plan. Nurse to provide orders.
